title: Claims Review Board Table: Repeat Limits, Appeals and Withdrawal for Delivery Claims
content:
Claims Review Board table of the per-type limits on Delivery Claims: how many claims of a type may be approved for one customer in a trailing 12 months, the evidence that lifts that limit, the appeal window and the number of appeals, and when a claim may be withdrawn.

| Claim type | Most claims of this type approved in a trailing 12 months before further ones are denied | Evidence that lets a claim over the limit be decided normally | Appeal window (calendar days after the decision date) | Appeal needs evidence logged after the denial | Appeals per claim | Withdrawal possible only before a decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Late Delivery Claim | 0 (no limit) | not applicable | 30 | yes | 1 | yes |
| Delivered Not Received Claim | 2 | a police report reference | 30 | yes | 1 | yes |
| Lost in Transit Claim | 0 (no limit) | not applicable | 30 | yes | 1 | yes |
| Damaged in Transit Claim | 0 (no limit) | not applicable | 30 | yes | 1 | yes |
| Missing Item Claim | 2 | a police report reference | 30 | yes | 1 | yes |
| Wrong Item Claim | 0 (no limit) | not applicable | 30 | yes | 1 | yes |

## Board notes

- Only two types carry a repeat limit: the Delivered Not Received Claim and the Missing Item Claim, each at 2 claims approved in a trailing 12 months. A 0 means there is no limit for that type.
- For those two types a police report reference on the claim lets a claim over the limit be decided normally.
- Every type allows 1 appeal, within 30 calendar days after the decision date, and the appeal needs evidence logged after the denial.
- Every type may be withdrawn only before a decision is made.
